name: Double Lexicographically Minimum
description: You are given a string $$$s$$$. You can reorder the characters to form a string $$$t$$$. Define $$$t_{\mathrm{max}}$$$ to be the lexicographical maximum of $$$t$$$ and $$$t$$$ in reverse order. Given $$$s$$$ determine the lexicographically minimum value of $$$t_{\mathrm{max}}$$$ over all reorderings $$$t$$$ of $$$s$$$. A string $$$a$$$ is lexicographically smaller than a string $$$b$$$ if and only if one of the following holds: $$$a$$$ is a prefix of $$$b$$$, but $$$a \ne b$$$; in the first position where $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ differ, the string $$$a$$$ has a letter that appears earlier in the alphabet than the corresponding letter in $$$b$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^5$$$) — the number of test cases. Descriptions of test cases follow. The first and only line of each test case contains a string $$$s$$$ ($$$1 \leq |s| \leq 10^5$$$). $$$s$$$ consists of only lowercase English letters. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$|s|$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case print the lexicographically minimum value of $$$t_{\mathrm{max}}$$$ over all reorderings $$$t$$$ of $$$s$$$.

approach_summary: Precompute the prefix function π[i] matching longest proper prefix-suffix in O(M). Traverse text string with π transitions to locate all occurrences in O(N) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1799C — Double Lexicographically Minimum [406. Knuth Morris Pratt (KMP) and Prefix Automaton]
topic_editorial.summary: String matching with prefix automaton / KMP.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The prefix function $\pi[i]$ defines the length of the longest proper prefix of $S[0..i]$ that is also a suffix of $S[0..i]$. When a mismatch occurs at index $j$, we do not backtrack in text; we jump to $\pi[j-1]$, preserving previously matched characters.
